notes: Both advertised tools are registered in `createMcpServer` without a feature flag or disabled-by-default toolset.

Although the tools are annotated read-only, the enforcement `kind` is WRITE here because the tool arguments are sent out of the agent context to the Context7 API as request parameters. The destination is fixed, so no `destination_args` are recorded and no SINK label is applied.

query-docs.rationale: `query-docs` is registered unconditionally and calls `fetchLibraryContext({ query, libraryId }, ctx)`. `fetchLibraryContext` sends `query` and `libraryId` to the Context7 API with generated headers and returns the upstream documentation text as `content[].text`. It is UNTRUSTED because the documentation corpus is described as community-contributed and may contain attacker-authored project content. It is SECRET when credentials are configured because API keys are documented as enabling private repository access, and the tool can return those credential-scoped docs. It is not a SINK because the upstream is fixed by the server code rather than chosen by the agent. No host execution is present.

resolve-library-id.rationale: `resolve-library-id` is registered unconditionally and calls `searchLibraries(query, libraryName, ctx)`. `searchLibraries` sends the caller's `query` and `libraryName` to the Context7 API with generated headers derived from the client context, and the returned JSON is formatted into `content[].text`. It is UNTRUSTED because Context7 projects/docs are described as community-contributed, so library names/descriptions/IDs in returned results may be attacker-controllable. It is SECRET when credentials are configured because the README states API keys enable access to private repositories, and the tool returns credential-scoped search results into the agent context. It is not a SINK under the stated rule because the destination is the fixed Context7 upstream, not an agent-chosen URL/host. No host code execution is present.

value_conditions.effect: In stdio mode, supplies `stdioApiKey`; when this flag and `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` are absent, credential-backed/private-repository SECRET access is not available by default. The flag is disallowed with `--transport http`.
In stdio mode, supplies `stdioApiKey` if `--api-key` is not set; absence removes credential-backed/private-repository SECRET access for stdio by default.

In HTTP mode, these headers supply `apiKey` in request context; absent headers mean unauthenticated `/mcp` requests can still run but without credential-backed/private-repository SECRET access, except on auth-required routes/clients.
value_conditions.syntax: Authorization: Bearer <key> | Authorization: <key> | X-Context7-API-Key: <key> | Context7-API-Key: <key> | X-API-Key: <key> | context7_api_key: <key> | x_api_key: <key>

value_conditions.default: /mcp is used for normal MCP traffic; /mcp/oauth is only used when selected by the client
value_conditions.effect: Requires authentication; without an accepted API key/JWT the request is rejected before tool execution. Authenticated calls may have credential-backed/private-repository SECRET access.
Selects stdio or HTTP transport. Both transports create the same server and register the same tools, so this does not remove tools or labels; default is stdio.
